compensating.why: hop 3 searches every slot of the table
hop 2 takes the key's hash code without the null rule

ownership_reason: Only the gold decides whether a slot holds the key: hop 1 packs the slots into arrays and turns the index into a boolean, hop 2 supplies the key's hash code (zero for a null key, as stored), hop 3 bounds the number of slots searched by the table length, hop 4 passes everything on. Once the gold compares the keys of the slots by identity, a key equal to but not the same object as the stored one (the read-back keys of a serialised map) can be found only if a caller replaces the probe by the stored object, which needs an equality search over the slots, or replaces the gold. The gold's javadoc promises the slot 'holding the specified key'; a map holds a key when one of its keys equals it (java.util.Map.containsKey), and the variant reports that the read-back map does not hold ONE. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact siblings Flat3Map.get, Flat3Map.put and Flat3Map.remove compare `hash == hashCode && key.equals(keyN)`, and the delegate map's rule is AbstractHashedMap.isEqualKey (`key1 == key2 || key1.equals(key2)`); TestFlat3Map::testCollections261 (remove finds keys put as other equal Integer objects) and TestFlat3Map::testSerialisation4 (the read-back map in delegate mode holds the equal keys) pass, as does TestFlat3Map::testClone2 through the chain.
